searchText: This means metadata is always written in runtime. Is this a feasible assumption? Doesn't the operation to append them to runtime code always have to be in the init code this way? AFAIK Vyper has the Vyper version metadata (not the metadata file) encoded in the runtime bytecode in CBOR This is cumbersome in legacy bytecode, especially for nested contracts: https://docs.sourcify.dev/blog/finding-auxdatas-in-bytecode/ Having the metadata appended in respective data sections would solve that issue for runtime codes but I'm not sure how that will work with the creation code, I'm still not fully familiar with the whole creation process. That still assumes metadata is always appended and CBOR encoded. And I can't point out an example but making it accessible to the code doesn't feel like a good practice. If you can trick the verifier, you can easily have some code that is not visible in the verified source code https://samczsun.com/hiding-in-plain-sight/ it's in the initcode! Any docs about that? I could only find https://github.com/vyperlang/vyper/issues/3549 discussion mm idk about docs, we can add some links to https://github.com/vyperlang/vyper/pull/3471 https://github.com/vyperlang/vyper/pulls?q=is%3Apr+cbor also these are pretty much all the PRs touching the cbor metadata
